resultados.refuerzo: ¡Atrévete! means dare to: an imperative that encourages someone to take a risk.
Cálmate means calm down, the opposite of encouraging someone to take a risk.
Perdona que takes the subjunctive, so moleste fits after the apology.
Molesto is an adjective; the sentence needs the subjunctive moleste.
Molestar is infinitive; after perdona que a conjugated subjunctive is needed.
Te lo mereces praises someone, which is out of place at a funeral; sympathy fits.
Tirando means getting by: neither well nor badly.
A wish with que takes the subjunctive, so pases is the right form.
Pasas is indicative; a wish with que needs the subjunctive, pases.
Pasarás is future; a wish with que needs the subjunctive, pases.
Perdona que takes the subjunctive, so interrumpa fits here.
Interrumpo is indicative; perdona que needs the subjunctive, interrumpa.
Interrumpir is infinitive; perdona que needs a conjugated subjunctive.
Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, so olvide is correct.
Olvida is indicative; antes de que always takes the subjunctive, olvide.
Olvidará is future; antes de que takes the subjunctive, olvide.
Por lo visto means apparently: it reports something you have only heard.
Le agradecería que takes the imperfect subjunctive, so enviara fits.
A continuación introduces the next part of a talk: next, in sequence.
En suma closes a talk with a summary; it does not announce the next part.
Concretamente narrows the focus to one exact case: specifically.
Bostezar means to yawn, which is what sleepy people do.
Estornudar means to sneeze, a reflex, not a sign of sleepiness.
Sudar means to sweat, which is not what sleepiness usually causes.
Both is wrong: the question asks which single brother is mean with money.
Repair costs is a distractor; the question asks what the siblings quarrelled about.
Yerno means son-in-law, the husband of your daughter.
Parientes means relatives, so the sentence says relatives in Argentina.
Early retirement is a distractor; the question asks why life expectancy rose.
Knowing him by sight is a distractor; the question asks her first impression.
Price is a distractor; the question asks why Spaniards follow the diet less.
Legumbres means pulses, the dried seeds of beans, lentils and chickpeas.
Speed is a distractor; the question asks why you should not stir too much.
Clay is a distractor; the question asks about the effect of stirring.
Estar is infinitive; hasta que needs a conjugated subjunctive, esté.
Expensive is a distractor; acogedor in an advert describes a cosy, welcoming home.
Al fontanero means the plumber, the person to call about a broken pipe.
A plazos means in instalments, paying a little each month.
Preferiría que takes the imperfect subjunctive, so cambiaran fits.
Renting is a distractor; the question asks why Olga doubted she could buy.
